newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa tumbles on fund liquidation.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa tumbles on fund liquidation.

text.p: Heavy fund long liquidation sent CSCE cocoa futures to their lowest level in a month Monday morning, traders said.
At 0930 EDT, May was down $78 at $1,395 a tonne, traded $1,452 to $1,390. Second-position July was $71 lower at $1,433, while the remaining months were down $21 to $63.

Prices gapped $25 lower at the outset on the heels of a weak performance in London overnight. Downward momentum accelerated after sell stops were touched off below $1,450 in May, with additional stops activated near $1,35 and $1,400.
Traders said speculators, who many players estimated to be net long by more than 30,000 lots, are liquidating positions ahead of the May contract's first notice day April 15.
May open interest remained hefty as of April 3 at 30,254 lots.

Traders said lackluster European grinds also contributed to the market's bearish tone. German Confectionery Industry Association BDS said Monday German cocoa grindings dropped by 11.71 percent to 61,379.3 tonnes in the first quarter of 1997 from 69,520.3 tonnes in the same 1996 period.
Although the decline was within analysts' expectations, traders said it was stll disappointing.
Analysts last week estimated the first quarter data to be down at perhaps 60,000 tonnes, citing extremely high year-ago figures.
-- Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk, 212 859 1640
